cards.explanation: The answer is that they cry out to Jesus for mercy. When they heard that Jesus was passing by, they cried out, "Lord, Son of David, have mercy on us!" (Matthew 20:30). They didn't whisper it or hint at it. I think these two knew a chance when they heard one, and they used their voices.

The crowd tells them to be silent. Matthew says, "The crowd admonished them to be silent…" (Matthew 20:31). That's a whole crowd telling two men to pipe down, friends. Imagine trying to shout your order at a counter while the whole line goes "shhhh."

The answer is that they cry out all the louder. "…they cried out all the louder, 'Lord, Son of David, have mercy on us!'" (Matthew 20:31). The crowd said hush, and these two turned the volume up. I wish I'd had that kind of nerve when somebody first slid that drawer shut on me.

The answer is that Jesus stops and calls them. Matthew says, "Jesus stopped and called them." (Matthew 20:32) A large crowd was following Him as He left Jericho (Matthew 20:29), and He stopped for two men sitting by the road. I think that tells you plenty about who gets His attention, friends.

The answer is eyes. "Lord," they answered, "let our eyes be opened." (Matthew 20:33). Jesus had just asked, "What do you want Me to do for you?" (Matthew 20:32), and they knew exactly what to say. No hemming, no hawing, bakers. They had their order ready.
The answer is False. Matthew 20:34 says, "…at once they received their sight…" There was no waiting, friends. Jesus touched their eyes, and they could see right then.

The answer is that they follow Jesus. Matthew 20:34 says they "…received their sight and followed Him." The first thing they did with their new eyes was walk behind Jesus. I think I'd have stared at my own hands for an hour first.
